background: DNB is Norway's largest bank, part-owned by the Norwegian state, funded by Norwegian deposits and covered bonds and lending to Norwegian households and companies, with a large shipping and energy book.
synthesis: Rated AA on average across two of the three, the weakest of them at AA-, both on a stable outlook, DNB is among the highest-rated banks in the comparison. Capital is the strength, with CET1 of 17.4% and leverage of 6.3% both above the median for EU and Nordic banks. Liquidity is the weak spot, with LCR of 136% and NSFR of 116% both in the bottom quarter. CET1 has fallen 1.6 points since 30 Jun 2024 while the other ratios have been broadly flat, and the only flagged item in the last 90 days, on 17 Jul 2026, is positive.
